subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Normal Puberty Sequence

steps.tx: **Hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis** reactivation marks the neuroendocrine onset of female puberty. Throughout childhood, the reproductive axis remains held under profound central GABAergic and neuropeptide Y inhibition. Pubertal initiation begins when kisspeptin, acting via the GPR54 (KISS1R) receptor on GnRH neurons, escapes central inhibition and triggers pulsatile release of gonadotropin-releasing hormone, initially occurring exclusively during nocturnal sleep. This pulsatile stimulus disinhibits anterior pituitary secretion of luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone, driving ovarian estrogen synthesis.
steps.say: Female puberty begins when kisspeptin awakens the dormant reproductive axis, releasing nocturnal pulses of GnRH. This stimulates pituitary LH and FSH to prompt ovarian estrogen production, setting physical changes into motion.

steps.tx: **Pubertal sequence** in females unfolds in a predictable, highly conserved chronological order spanning three to four years, remembered by the clinical mnemonic T-A-P-M: Thelarche (breast budding), Adrenarche/Pubarche (pubic and axillary hair), Peak height velocity (maximum growth spurt), and Menarche (onset of menstruation). Disruption of this sequence, such as menarche preceding breast thelarche, represents a red flag pointing to exogenous estrogen exposure, ovarian neoplasms, or adrenal virilization.
steps.say: Female puberty follows a precise four-stage sequence: Thelarche breast budding comes first, followed by Pubarche pubic hair, Peak height velocity, and finally Menarche. Any deviation from this order demands investigation.

steps.tx: **Thelarche** is the appearance of palpable glandular breast buds beneath the areola, representing the earliest outward physical manifestation of true female puberty. Emerging at an average age of 8.5 to 10.5 years, it is driven by ovarian estradiol synthesis under pituitary FSH stimulation. Clinically defined as Tanner stage B2, the subareolar bud is frequently unilateral and tender initially, a normal physiological asymmetry that requires parental reassurance rather than imaging or surgical excision.
steps.say: Thelarche is the appearance of palpable breast buds, the very first physical sign of puberty. It typically begins between eight and ten years of age and is often asymmetrical, which is completely physiological.

vis.title: Tanner Staging System for Female Breast Development
rows: Elevation of papilla only (no glandular tissue)
Palpable breast bud beneath enlarged areola
Areola and papilla project to form secondary mound

steps.tx: **Adrenarche** and pubarche describe the development of coarse, pigmented pubic hair and axillary hair under the influence of weak adrenal androgens, predominantly dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) and androstenedione from the expanding adrenal zona reticularis. While pubarche normally follows thelarche by six to twelve months, adrenarche represents an independent maturation of the adrenal cortex that is not driven by pituitary gonadotropins and occurs independently of ovarian follicular activation.
steps.say: Pubarche brings coarse pubic and axillary hair about six to twelve months after breast budding. It is driven by adrenal androgens like DHEA from the adrenal cortex, rather than pituitary gonadotropins.

left.title: Thelarche (Ovarian)
points: Ovarian estradiol stimulates breast ductal growth
Correlates with bone age and growth acceleration
Essential marker of true central puberty

right.title: Adrenarche (Adrenal)
points: Driven by adrenal zona reticularis maturation
Does not indicate true gonadal puberty

steps.tx: **Peak height velocity** occurs early in female puberty, peaking at Tanner stage 3 at an average age of 11.5 to 12 years, approximately six to twelve months prior to menarche. Under the synergistic stimulation of rising estrogen levels and accelerated growth hormone secretion, girls achieve a maximum linear growth rate averaging 8 to 9 centimetres per year. Once menarche arrives, high circulating estrogen levels promote epiphyseal growth plate senescence, leaving minimal residual growth.
steps.say: The female growth spurt happens early in puberty, peaking before menarche at eight to nine centimetres per year. Once menarche occurs, high estrogen levels fuse epiphyseal plates, leaving only a few centimetres of growth.

steps.tx: **Menarche** represents the onset of the first menstrual period, arriving as a late pubertal milestone at an average age of 12.8 years, typically at Tanner breast stage 4. Menarche occurs approximately 2 to 2.5 years following the initial appearance of thelarche. Most menstrual cycles during the first one to two years following menarche are anovulatory due to immaturity of positive estrogen feedback on the hypothalamic LH surge mechanism, presenting with physiological cycle irregularity.
steps.say: Menarche arrives late in the sequence, about two and a half years after thelarche, at an average age of twelve point eight years. Cycles are normally irregular and anovulatory for the first two years due to hypothalamic immaturity.

left.title: Early Post-Menarcheal State
points: Anovulatory cycles in over fifty percent
Cycle intervals vary widely (21 to 45 days)

steps.tx: **Precocious puberty** is formally defined as the development of secondary sexual characteristics prior to the age of eight years in girls. It is categorized into central (GnRH-dependent) precocious puberty, where premature activation of the hypothalamic HPG axis produces an orderly pubertal sequence with elevated LH, and peripheral (GnRH-independent) precocious puberty, where autonomous sex steroid secretion from ovarian follicular cysts, granulosa cell tumours, or adrenal lesions suppresses gonadotropins.
steps.say: Precocious puberty is defined as pubertal signs before age eight. Central precocious puberty is GnRH-dependent and follows the normal orderly sequence, whereas peripheral precocious puberty is driven by ovarian or adrenal tumours with suppressed gonadotropins.

vis.title: Classification of Precocious Puberty in Girls
rows: Autonomous ovarian or adrenal steroid secretion
Suppressed basal LH and FSH (<0.1 IU/L)
Normal prepubertal bone age and hormones

steps.tx: **Delayed puberty** is diagnosed when there is a complete absence of breast budding (thelarche) by thirteen years of age, or an absence of menarche by fifteen years of age in the presence of normal secondary sexual development. Constitutional delay of growth and puberty is the most common benign etiology, characterized by delayed bone age and a family history. Pathological causes include hypergonadotropic hypogonadism, most commonly Turner syndrome (45,X), and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism from Kallmann syndrome.
steps.say: Delayed puberty is defined by absent breast thelarche by age thirteen, or absent menarche by age fifteen. Constitutional delay is the most common benign cause, while Turner syndrome is the leading genetic cause.

nodes.label: Delayed Milestones
nodes.sub: No thelarche by 13 or no menses by 15

nodes.label: Measure LH and FSH
nodes.sub: Differentiates primary gonadal from central failure
